The Act provides for commencement by a separate Central Government notification.

questions.subtopic: Case Analysis: VB-G RAM G Rural Asset Creation
questions.question: In a drought-prone village, 80 eligible rural workers are engaged in a water-conservation project under the VB-G RAM G framework. Which pair of outcomes best describes the purpose of such work?
options: Draining groundwater to create private resorts
Forcing all villagers to leave agriculture permanently
Eliminating the need for future irrigation
Providing wage employment within the household-based statutory guarantee while creating a durable water-conservation asset
questions.explanation: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 provides a guarantee of not less than 125 days of wage employment per covered rural household, subject to statutory conditions. Its framework also links employment to durable rural assets, including works supporting water conservation and resilience. The guarantee is not 125 days for each individual worker.

questions.subtopic: Case Analysis: Biscuit Production Supply Chain
questions.question: A packet of biscuits is manufactured using flour, sugar, vegetable oil, and packaging paper. In computing national income, why is the statistician instructed to include only the retail price of the biscuit packet?
options: Because agricultural wheat has no monetary value until it reaches the consumer
Because counting the separate sales of wheat, flour, sugar, and oil before the biscuit is sold would count the same value multiple times, artificially inflating GDP
Because biscuit manufacturers do not pay income taxes to the government
Because intermediate goods are not traded in market economies
questions.explanation: Intermediate values are completely absorbed within the final product. Counting both intermediate inputs and final goods creates the classic GDP error of double counting.

questions.subtopic: Informal Workers in Urban Construction
questions.question: Construction workers gathering at urban labour chowks each morning to seek daily work illustrate which employment reality?
options: Permanent tenured employment in the public sector
Regular organised-sector employment with assured monthly salaries
Software consultancy employment in IT parks
Precarious daily-wage work where hiring and earnings depend on daily demand and workers may lack regular employment benefits
questions.explanation: Daily hiring at labour chowks illustrates irregular and insecure work. The example does not establish that every worker lacks every form of safety equipment or statutory compensation; actual protections depend on the applicable law and employment arrangement.

questions.subtopic: Government Support for Small Scale Industries
questions.question: Why does the central government provide marketing support, subsidized raw materials, and institutional credit to small scale industries (SSIs)?
options: Because small scale industries are highly labour-intensive and generate substantial manufacturing employment across tier-2 and tier-3 towns
Because small scale industries produce heavy nuclear submarines
Because small scale industries are owned exclusively by state governments
Because multinational corporations refuse to sell consumer goods
questions.explanation: Small-scale industries are crucial for decentralized industrialization and employment generation because they absorb more labour per unit of capital than large mega-factories.

questions.subtopic: Tertiary Sector Growth Engine
questions.question: Which of the following factors best explains why the expansion of agriculture and industry directly accelerates tertiary service growth?
options: Agriculture and industry destroy service sector employment
Farmers stop buying clothes once crop harvests increase
Greater farm and factory production requires more transport trucks, commercial warehouses, banking credit, and marketing retail distribution
Factory workers refuse to use commercial transport networks
questions.explanation: The development of agriculture and industry leads to the development of services such as transport, trade, and storage. The greater the development of primary and secondary sectors, the greater the demand for such services.

questions.subtopic: Public Sector Health and Education Obligations
questions.question: Why does NCERT identify the provision of quality basic education and healthcare as an important responsibility of the government?
options: Because private hospitals are legally barred from treating patients
Because private schools are constitutionally prohibited
Because the government must help ensure access to essential services and human development, including for people who may not be able to afford adequate provision privately
Because all private providers are prohibited from charging fees
questions.explanation: NCERT emphasises the government's responsibility to provide health and education facilities for all and to address wider human-development needs such as safe drinking water, housing, food and nutrition. Private providers may also operate; public responsibility is to help ensure broad and equitable access.

questions.subtopic: Synthesis: Policy Blueprint for Sectoral Health
questions.question: To achieve balanced, inclusive, and employment-rich economic growth, which integrated strategy must India execute across its sectors?
options: Shut down all primary agricultural farming and import all food grains from abroad
Nationalize all private corporate software companies and dismantle private enterprises
Abolish all labour welfare laws to eliminate the organised sector completely
Modernize agriculture and agro-processing, stimulate labour-intensive manufacturing, expand affordable credit and skill development, and formalize unorganised worker protections
questions.explanation: Sustainable development requires agricultural productivity gains, expanding job-rich manufacturing, formalizing unorganised workers, and providing universal public health and education.
